transcript.note: Round 1 — leaves first. The gridding output puts all 59 vertices on 59 distinct rows AND 59 distinct columns, so hv=0 by construction: no two adjacent points share a coordinate anywhere. Degree-1 points are the cheapest and safest place to buy H/V: they carry a single segment, so snapping one cannot break any other alignment, and rule (4) winding order is unchecked at the leaf itself. I took all 14 of the 16 leaves whose single neighbour sits within +/-3 on one axis, choosing V on ties per the criteria: 0->(24,14) V under 20; 21->(47,3) V over 6; 8->(4,6) V under 47; 14->(1,4) V over 48; 19->(25,51) V under 27; 52->(10,58) V under 49; 56->(7,55) V over 57; and H where it is strictly nearer: 1->(23,2) with 3, 5->(41,8) with 6, 29->(12,52) with 51, 41->(54,34) with 30, 46->(56,22) with 22, 54->(55,16) with 53. 37 is the one exception: the H snap to (29,13) would have wound 37 past neighbour 2 in the bearing order around interchange 18 (-26.6deg -> 0deg crossing 2 at -14deg), so I took the V snap to (27,12) instead, which lands at -90deg and leaves 18's cyclic order [37,2,38,20] intact. Leaves 42 and 43 are unreachable (13/4 and 11/7 cells from their neighbours) and stay put.
